Apple today released iOS 26.6.1, bringing a new software update to iPhone that fixes over 20 security vulnerabilities. Details below.

Apple releases security update notes for iOS 26.6.1 and other systems

Although iOS 27 is about to launch, Apple today still released a security-focused software update for iOS 26 and its companion platforms including macOS and visionOS.

iOS 26.6.1 is now available, and according to Apple's security update notes, it fixes more than 20 security vulnerabilities on iPhone.

Most of the fixes involve WebKit, but also include patches for audio, ImageIO, the core system (Kernel), and more.

You can check the full security details through the link below:

visionOS 26.6.1 update notes have not yet been released. Apple's official website only states they will be "published later." However, the vast majority of content is expected to be the same as Apple's other platforms.

With iOS 27 expected to launch in just a few weeks, today's update is likely to be the last one we'll see before iOS 27 rolls out.

Apple previously stated that it plans to release software updates containing security patches more frequently in the future. This is due to the increasing risk of AI-driven hacking attacks.
